report.summary: Portfolio screen failures since 13:43 are caused by a memory leak in portfolio-service v3.8.0 (chg-7001) which keeps per-user holdings snapshots in memory without proper eviction. This caused memory exhaustion, pod OOMKills, and sidecar log-shipping termination, which explains why application logs appeared clean.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Memory leak in portfolio-service v3.8.0 deployment

supporting.note: v3.8.0 introduced in-memory per-user holdings snapshots
Kubernetes logged multiple OOMKilled events for portfolio-service containers
fluent-bit sidecar OOMKilled, explaining why application logs appeared clean/empty

contradicting.note: Request rate remained stable without anomalous surge
Client BFF request rate remained completely normal

facts.text: portfolio-service v3.8.0 was deployed on 2026-10-08 at 18:20 with summary 'keep per-user holdings snapshots in memory'.
portfolio-service memory usage hit 106.64% saturation at 13:44.
portfolio-service and mobile-bff error rates spiked starting around 13:40-13:43.
Kubernetes logged portfolio-service pods and fluent-bit being OOMKilled starting at 13:40.

assumptions: The holdings snapshots kept in memory lack proper TTL or LRU eviction policies, leading to unbounded growth.
The lack of application logs was entirely due to the fluent-bit sidecar being OOMKilled.
evidence_gaps: Application-level exception stack traces were unavailable due to fluent-bit OOMKill.

timeline.event: portfolio-service v3.8.0 deployed with in-memory per-user holdings snapshots

recommended_actions.rationale: Removes the memory leak introduced in v3.8.0 and restores portfolio screen stability.

recommended_actions.action: Restart or adjust fluent-bit sidecar memory limits
recommended_actions.rationale: Restores log shipping to inspect application logs correctly.

recommended_actions.action: Implement proper cache bounds/eviction or externalize caching to redis-cache
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents future container OOMs when holding snapshots in memory.
